title: Five a Day? Not Even Close

pre.en: What does Dr Webster's question at the end suggest?
pre.zh: Webster 博士最后那句反问说明了什么？
options: She hadn't eaten many portions herself.
She ate a lot of vegetables that day.

intro: 一段电台式的健康小报道：主持人先问听众昨天吃了几份蔬果，再给调查数字，讲利兹一家公司的小办法，最后引专家的原话。读的时候留意 be used to doing（已经习惯）和 get used to doing（渐渐习惯）：这里的 to 是介词，后面接 doing。结尾有个小笑点。

sentences.en: Here's a question for you: how many portions of fruit and veg did you eat yesterday?
sentences.zh: 先问大家一个问题：你昨天吃了几份水果蔬菜？

sentences.en: If the answer's five, well done, because you're doing better than most of us.
sentences.zh: 如果是五份，那恭喜你，你比我们大多数人都强。

sentences.en: A new survey has found that only one in three UK adults eats five portions a day.
sentences.zh: 一项新调查发现，英国成年人里只有三分之一每天能吃够五份。

sentences.en: The typical adult manages 3.7, and lots of people fall well short of the target.
sentences.zh: 普通成年人每天吃 3.7 份，很多人离这个目标还差得远。

sentences.en: I spoke to Dr Karen Webster at the University of Leeds, who led the study of two thousand people.
sentences.zh: 我采访了利兹大学的 Karen Webster 博士，这项覆盖两千人的调查就是她牵头做的。

sentences.en: She says people do know what a balanced diet looks like.
sentences.zh: 她说，大家其实知道均衡饮食是什么样的。

sentences.en: "Most people keep meaning to eat better," she told me.
sentences.zh: 「大多数人一直都打算吃得健康点，」她跟我说。

sentences.en: "They just aren't used to eating vegetables at breakfast or lunch."
sentences.zh: 「只是不习惯早饭、午饭的时候吃蔬菜。」

sentences.en: "On top of that, a lot of the snacks we reach for at work are high in sugar."
sentences.zh: 「再加上，我们上班时随手拿的零食，很多含糖量都很高。」

sentences.en: So one insurance office in Leeds has tried something simple.
sentences.zh: 于是，利兹的一家保险公司试了个简单的办法。

sentences.en: The manager, Gary Pike, got permission to spend fifteen pounds a week on fruit.
sentences.zh: 经理 Gary Pike 申请到了每周 15 英镑的水果钱。

sentences.en: Every Monday, he puts a big bowl of apples, pears and bananas next to the kettle.
sentences.zh: 每周一，他都在烧水壶旁边摆上一大碗苹果、梨和香蕉。

sentences.en: "Before, we'd snack on biscuits all afternoon," he says.
sentences.zh: 「以前我们一下午都在吃饼干，」他说。

sentences.en: "When you're busy, you lose track of time and eat whatever's nearest."
sentences.zh: 「一忙起来就忘了时间，手边有什么就吃什么。」

sentences.en: Within a month, most of the team had got used to having an apple at four o'clock.
sentences.zh: 不到一个月，团队里大多数人都习惯了下午四点吃个苹果。

sentences.en: Some people even bring fruit along from their own gardens.
sentences.zh: 有人还从自家园子里带水果过来。

sentences.en: And the biscuit tin?
sentences.zh: 那饼干罐呢？

sentences.en: It's been handed over to the cleaners.
sentences.zh: 已经转交给保洁阿姨了。

sentences.en: One of his team told me, "I'm still not used to seeing my boss eat a pear."
sentences.zh: 他手下一个人跟我说：「看老板吃梨，我到现在还不太习惯。」

sentences.en: Dr Webster says small changes like this go a long way.
sentences.zh: Webster 博士说，这样的小改变作用很大。

sentences.en: "People go on about expensive superfoods, but frozen peas are just as good for you," she says.
sentences.zh: 「大家老念叨那些贵得要命的超级食物，其实冷冻豌豆对身体一样好，」她说。

sentences.en: "You don't have to be perfect."
sentences.zh: 「不用做到完美。」

sentences.en: "And you'll get used to less sugar surprisingly fast."
sentences.zh: 「而且你会发现，少吃糖，适应起来快得出乎意料。」

sentences.en: At the end of our chat, I asked how many portions she'd had that day.
sentences.zh: 聊到最后，我问她那天吃了几份蔬果。

sentences.en: Dr Webster paused.
sentences.zh: Webster 博士顿了一下。

sentences.en: "Does ketchup count?"
sentences.zh: 「番茄酱算吗？」

cards.note: 英国的 five a day 指每天五份蔬果，一份大约 80 克，比如一个苹果。
做调查是 carry out a survey；名词重音在前 SUR-vey。

cards.zh: 没达到（目标、要求）；差一截
cards.note: to fail to reach a target or the amount you need
cards.tip: 中间可以加 well、just 说差多少：fall just short（差一点）。fall 的过去式 fell，过去分词 fallen。
cards.example: Sales fell short of what we expected this year.

cards.note: a way of eating that includes the right amounts of different kinds of food
cards.tip: diet 在这里是「日常饮食」，不一定是减肥；「在节食」才是 be on a diet。
cards.example: A balanced diet doesn't mean you can never eat chocolate.

cards.note: to plan to do something many times but not actually do it
in addition to something, especially something difficult
to contain a lot of something, such as sugar, fat or salt
cards.tip: 反义是 be low in sth；介词用 in，不用 of。
cards.example: These crisps are very high in salt.

cards.note: to be told officially that you can do something
cards.tip: permission 不可数，不加 a；向谁要用 ask (sb) for permission。
cards.example: We got permission to leave early on Friday.

cards.note: 和 pair（一双）、bear（熊）押韵，读 /peə/。
to eat small amounts of a particular food between meals
cards.tip: snack 可以当动词；不说 eat snack on。
cards.example: I try to snack on nuts instead of crisps.

cards.zh: 忘了时间；不知不觉过了很久
cards.note: to forget what time it is because you are busy or interested in something
to take someone or something with you when you go somewhere
cards.tip: 代词放中间：bring it along；bring 的过去式是 brought。
cards.example: Feel free to bring a friend along on Saturday.

cards.note: to give work or responsibility for something to another person
to be very helpful in improving a situation
cards.tip: 也说钱「很经花」：Ten pounds goes a long way here。别按字面理解成「走很远」。
cards.example: A quick thank-you email goes a long way.

cards.note: to talk about something for a long time, often in a way that is boring for other people
cards.tip: 带点不耐烦；后面接名词或 doing。
cards.example: He keeps going on about his new car.

cards.zh: 超级食物（据说特别有营养的食物）
cards.note: 广告里常见，比如牛油果、奇亚籽，带点营销味。
freeze（冷冻）的过去分词：freeze–froze–frozen。
单数 pea；英国人家里冰箱几乎都有一袋冻豌豆。
to be healthy for you to eat or do
cards.tip: 对身体不好是 be bad for you；注意介词 for，不说 good to you（那是「对你好、待你好」）。
cards.example: Walking to work is good for you and saves money.

cards.note: to talk with someone in a friendly, informal way
英国人也常说 tomato sauce。
